paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive disorder. It presents in infancy or childhood with severe thrombocytopenia and reduced or absent bone marrow megakaryocytes, and it can progress to trilineage bone marrow failure. Serum thrombopoietin is absent or inappropriately normal. THPO is produced outside hematopoietic cells, so the marrow failure does not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, but it does respond to thrombopoietin receptor agonists (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018).

checks.explanation: Biallelic or homozygous causation implies autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.evidence_quote: The disorder should be suspected in children or young adults presenting with hypo‐megakaryocytic thrombocytopenia with or without other peripheral cytopenias

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported 3 affected sibs born to first-cousin parents of Egyptian origin. The proband was a boy who presented in July 2009, at age 3.5 years, with ecchymotic patches. On examination he had preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. Blood counts showed very severe thrombocytopenia with normal platelet size, hyporegenerative anemia (reticulocyte count 22.8 x 10(9)/l), and severe neutropenia. The bone marrow was hypocellular, with very rare immature megakaryocytes. He had recurrent epistaxis, gum bleeding, and rectal bleeding, as well as recurrent febrile neutropenia and otitis media. Chromosome breakage testing excluded Fanconi anemia. His serum THPO was 10.9 pg/ml, which was not increased. His brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia at age 7 months, with normal peripheral blood cell morphology and a markedly decreased number of bone marrow megakaryocytes. From age 1.6 years the brother had recurrent spontaneous bleeding that required platelet transfusions; his serum THPO was 14.1 pg/ml. Their sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at age 2 months and was found to have anemia and severe thrombocytopenia with normal blood cell morphology. The parents had normal blood counts. Pecci et al. (2018) noted that the oldest sib had trilineage marrow hypoplasia, whereas the younger sibs had isolated thrombocytopenia or thrombocytopenia with anemia. They suggested that the hematologic picture worsens with age and is indistinguishable from CAMT caused by MPL mutations.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) reported a Muslim Palestinian boy (II-3) born to consanguineous parents. He presented at age 3.5 years with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (platelet count 21 x 10(9)/L) with a normal mean platelet volume. Bone marrow examination of 2 separate biopsies showed normocellular marrow with severe megakaryocyte hypoplasia, a few small immature forms, and mild dyserythropoiesis, consistent with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia. He also had mild, occasional neutropenia and urethral stenosis, but no pancytopenia. His serum thrombopoietin was 126 pg/mL, which was inappropriately normal to slightly elevated.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.112C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene, which they called R17C. Both parents and 1 heterozygous sib had reduced platelet counts, whereas a sib with the wildtype sequence had a normal platelet count. Media containing the mutant THPO were 2- to 3-fold less able to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells. In silico modeling predicted that adding a fifth cysteine to the receptor-binding domain, which contains 4 conserved cysteines forming 2 disulfide bonds, might disrupt normal disulfide bonding and impair receptor binding. Dasouki et al. (2013) concluded that this partial loss-of-function allele caused aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state.

paragraphs.text: In 3 sibs from a consanguineous Egyptian family with CAMT2, Pecci et al. (2018) found no variants in MPL and identified a homozygous c.355C-T mutation in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The parents were heterozygous for the mutation. Residue R119 lies in helix C of the MPL-binding domain and is conserved across species and in EPO. In transfected HEK293T cells, the mutant protein was expressed and stable, but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower than wildtype, suggesting impaired secretion. The previously reported R38C mutant behaved similarly. At equal concentrations, R119C THPO retained about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of UT7-TPO cells, and it caused defective activation of STAT5, ERK1/2, and AKT downstream of MPL.

paragraphs.text: In a Muslim Palestinian boy with CAMT2 born to consanguineous parents, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C-T variant (NM_000460.2; chr3:g.184096040G-A) in the promoter region of the THPO gene. The parents and a younger sib were heterozygous, and 2 healthy sibs were homozygous for the wildtype allele. The heterozygous mother and sib had asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia. In HEK293T cells, the variant reduced promoter reporter activity by almost 80%. In chromatin immunoprecipitation assays, it impaired binding of the transcription factors ETS1 and STAT4 to the THPO promoter. Knockdown of ETS1 and STAT4 in HepG2 cells reduced THPO mRNA and protein, and the 2 factors were shown to interact by proximity ligation and coimmunoprecipitation.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) found that serum THPO levels in 2 affected sibs were within the normal range, which was inappropriately low for their megakaryocyte-platelet mass. By contrast, levels are markedly increased in CAMT caused by MPL mutations. They suggested that measuring serum THPO could distinguish THPO-mutant CAMT from MPL-related CAMT and from other marrow failure syndromes.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) found that serum THPO levels in 2 sibs affected with CAMT2 were within the normal range.
checks.evidence_quote: Thrombopoietin levels measured in the sera of the two older siblings collected before romiplostim administration were within the normal range.

checks.claim: The normal serum THPO levels in the 2 sibs reported by Pecci et al. (2018) were inappropriately low for their megakaryocyte-platelet mass.
checks.evidence_quote: the serum THPO concentration was not increased in our patients and thus inappropriately lower than expected on the basis of their megakaryocyte–platelet mass

checks.claim: Serum THPO levels are markedly increased in CAMT caused by MPL mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: it is always markedly increased in all forms of bone marrow aplasia‐hypoplasia, including the CAMT form caused by MPL mutations

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) suggested that measuring serum THPO could distinguish THPO-mutant CAMT from MPL-related CAMT and from other marrow failure syndromes.
checks.evidence_quote: These observations suggest that measurement of the serum THPO level could be useful to discriminate CAMT patients with THPO mutations from those with MPL variants or other bone marrow failure syndromes.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) suggested that serum THPO measurement could serve as a screening tool, because a normal serum THPO level in a patient with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest a THPO defect. They recommended that the routine workup for suspected CAMT include analysis of THPO, including its regulatory regions.

checks.claim: Capaci et al. (2023) suggested that serum THPO measurement could serve as a screening tool for THPO defects.
checks.evidence_quote: we suggest that measurement of serum THPO concentration could be a valuable screening tool to recognize patients with THPO mutations

checks.claim: Capaci et al. (2023) suggested that a normal serum THPO level in a patient with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest a THPO defect.
checks.evidence_quote: The finding of a normal serum THPO level in the context of an amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest an alteration of THPO.

checks.claim: Capaci et al. (2023) recommended that the routine workup for suspected CAMT include analysis of THPO, including its regulatory regions.
checks.evidence_quote: molecular analysis of the THPO gene, including its regulatory regions, should be routinely included in the diagnostic workup of patients with a clinical suspicion of CAMT

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) reported that 4 children with THPO-related bone marrow failure who received hematopoietic stem cell transplants all had poor graft function. Their severe cytopenias persisted even after repeated transplants from different donors. In the 2 surviving patients, treatment with a THPO receptor agonist improved trilineage hematopoiesis.

checks.evidence_quote: Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function

checks.claim: Severe cytopenias persisted in the children with THPO-related bone marrow failure even after repeated transplants from different donors.
checks.evidence_quote: all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors

checks.claim: In the 2 surviving patients with THPO-related bone marrow failure reported by Seo et al. (2017), treatment with a THPO receptor agonist improved trilineage hematopoiesis.
checks.evidence_quote: For the 2 surviving patients, improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis was achieved following treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) treated all 3 affected sibs with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim. All 3 had trilineage hematologic responses, their bleeding and infections remitted, and transfusion independence was maintained for up to 6.5 years without side effects. The authors noted that HSCT is not expected to be effective because THPO is produced outside hematopoietic cells.

checks.evidence_quote: The three affected children were all treated with romiplostim, resulting in sustained trilineage response

checks.claim: Transfusion independence was maintained for up to 6.5 years without side effects in the 3 sibs treated with romiplostim by Pecci et al. (2018).

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) noted that HSCT is not expected to be effective in THPO-related CAMT because THPO is produced outside hematopoietic cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells, these patients are not expected to benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) treated a boy with CAMT2 due to a homozygous THPO promoter variant with eltrombopag. At 2.8 mg/kg/day, his platelet count rose gradually to 125 x 10(9)/L and his bruising resolved. This was the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.

checks.evidence_quote: He was therefore started on eltrombopag 1.4 mg/kg/day
checks.explanation: The proband with the homozygous promoter variant was treated with eltrombopag.

checks.claim: At an eltrombopag dose of 2.8 mg/kg/day, the platelet count of the boy reported by Capaci et al. (2023) rose gradually to 125 x 10(9)/L.
checks.evidence_quote: the dose was increased to 2.8 mg/kg/day. The patient's platelet count continues to increase gradually after 6 months of treatment at this dose; at the latest analysis, his platelet count was 125x109/L.

checks.claim: The bruising of the boy reported by Capaci et al. (2023) resolved with eltrombopag treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: At present, he is clinically well and no longer has easy bruising.

checks.claim: Capaci et al. (2023) was the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.

recurrent febrile neutropenia and otitis media
hypocellular bone marrow with very rare immature megakaryocytes

paragraphs.text: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) identified a homozygous c.112C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arginine-to-cysteine substitution, which they called R17C (residue 38). The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing. Both parents and 1 heterozygous sib had reduced platelet counts, whereas a wildtype sib had a normal platelet count. Media containing the mutant THPO were 2- to 3-fold less able to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells.

checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: A C>T change is a transition, and the abstract and title describe the patients.

checks.explanation: The paper gives both residue numbers: 38 counting the signal peptide and 17 excluding it.

paragraphs.text: In 3 sibs with CAMT2 born to first-cousin parents of Egyptian origin, Pecci et al. (2018) identified a homozygous c.355C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The parents were heterozygous. The mutant protein was expressed and stable in HEK293T cells, but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower than wildtype. At equal concentrations it retained about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of UT7-TPO cells, and it caused defective activation of STAT5, ERK1/2, and AKT.

paragraphs.text: In a Muslim Palestinian boy with CAMT2 born to consanguineous parents, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C-T variant (NM_000460.2) in the THPO promoter. The parents and a younger sib were heterozygous and had mild thrombocytopenia, and 2 healthy sibs were homozygous wildtype. In HEK293T cells, the variant reduced promoter reporter activity by almost 80%. It also impaired binding of ETS1 and STAT4 to the THPO promoter.
